definitions.def: to make something better or greater in value or quality
to meet or come across something by chance
a sudden clear understanding of something
causing damage or injury to something

grammar_choice.en_template: Suppose you {{1:have been working/have been worked}} on the solution to a challenging technological problem {{2:for/since}} many years.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 여러분이 어려운 기술적 문제의 해결책을 여러 해 동안 연구해 왔다고 가정해 보라.
explain: work는 능동의 현재완료진행 — have been working.

grammar_choice.en_template: Let's also suppose that you have been paying attention to {{1:whatever/whichever}} else you have encountered that {{2:might/may have}} be related to the problem.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 또한 여러분이 그 문제와 관련이 있을 수 있는, 마주친 그 밖의 무엇이든 주의를 기울여 왔다고 가정해 보자.
explain: 뒤에 동사원형 be가 오므로 조동사 might.

grammar_choice.en_template: In that case, chances are {{1:that/what}} creative solutions to the problem could suddenly pop up in your mind when you {{2:are/will be}} relaxed.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그런 경우, 여러분이 편안할 때 그 문제에 대한 창의적인 해결책이 갑자기 머릿속에 떠오를 가능성이 있다.
explain: chances are 뒤 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사 that.
시간 부사절(when)에서는 현재형이 미래를 대신 — are.

grammar_choice.en_template: Such "eureka moments" (when great insights {{1:lead/leads}} to discovery or invention) often {{2:take/takes}} place at unexpected times.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러한 "유레카 순간"(위대한 통찰이 발견이나 발명으로 이어지는 때)은 흔히 예상치 못한 때에 일어난다.

grammar_choice.en_template: To enhance spontaneous creativity, therefore, one must pay attention to the things {{1:that/what}} could potentially {{2:lead/leading}} to valuable outcomes.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 그러므로, 자발적인 창의성을 높이려면, 사람은 잠재적으로 가치 있는 결과로 이어질 수 있는 것들에 주의를 기울여야 한다.
explain: 선행사 the things를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that.

grammar_choice.en_template: This does not mean {{1:that/what}} you must {{2:narrow/narrowing}} down your interest to one specific topic.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 이것은 여러분이 자신의 관심을 하나의 특정 주제로 좁혀야 한다는 것을 의미하지 않는다.
explain: mean의 목적어 명사절을 이끄는 접속사 that.

grammar_choice.en_template: On the contrary, breadth of experience {{1:is/are}} the {{2:key/keys}} to creativity.
explain: the ~ to creativity, 단수 보어 key.

grammar_choice.en_template: If your experience {{1:is/being}} limited to a narrow range of topics, then the scope of your imagination will likewise be narrow, {{2:which/that}} would be harmful to creativity.
grammar_choice.ko_full: 만약 여러분의 경험이 좁은 범위의 주제에 한정된다면, 그러면 여러분의 상상력의 범위도 마찬가지로 좁아질 것이고, 이는 창의성에 해로울 것이다.
explain: 조건절의 정상 동사 형태 — is(수동 is limited).
앞 절 전체를 받는 계속적 용법 관계대명사 which.

jumble.answer: Suppose you have been working on the solution to a challenging technological problem for many years.
Let's also suppose that you have been paying attention to whatever else you have encountered that might be related to the problem.
In that case, chances are that creative solutions to the problem could suddenly pop up in your mind when you are relaxed.
Such "eureka moments" (when great insights lead to discovery or invention) often take place at unexpected times.
To enhance spontaneous creativity, therefore, one must pay attention to the things that could potentially lead to valuable outcomes.
This does not mean that you must narrow down your interest to one specific topic.
On the contrary, breadth of experience is the key to creativity.
If your experience is limited to a narrow range of topics, then the scope of your imagination will likewise be narrow, which would be harmful to creativity.
